expected: A replacement Build Spec may either use a non-cumulative delta list (historical convention) or retain some predecessor delta IDs as cumulative provenance. Activation validation must classify only delta IDs present in both predecessor and replacement manifests as inherited; every other listed delta is newly introduced and must satisfy the immediate previous-baseline/current-source checks.
actual: validate-activation.mjs requires every approved_delta_id in the new manifest/activation to have affected_build_spec equal the immediate previous baseline and to match the new activation source. BS-P1-005 correctly retains inherited BD-003/BD-004 provenance from BS-P1-004 and adds BD-005 for the BS-P1-004→005 change, so the current validator would falsely reject the inherited deltas.
evidence: BD-003/BD-004 describe the earlier BS-P1-003→BS-P1-004 remediation; BD-005 is the only new delta affecting BS-P1-004.
harness/scripts/validate-activation.mjs currently applies affected_build_spec/source provenance checks indiscriminately to every activation delta.
Historical baseline manifests are non-cumulative: BS-P1-002=[BD-001], BS-P1-003=[BD-002], BS-P1-004=[BD-003,BD-004]; therefore predecessor delta omission is valid repository history.

attempts.evidence: Dropping or rewriting inherited deltas would falsify the lineage of semantics already incorporated in BS-P1-004.

requested_planning_action: Classify inherited deltas as the intersection of predecessor and replacement approved_delta_ids; do not require a replacement baseline to repeat every predecessor delta.
Apply immediate previous-baseline affected_build_spec and current-source provenance checks only to delta IDs newly introduced by the replacement baseline.
Add attack cases for valid cumulative-delta rebaseline, valid non-cumulative replacement lineage, and forged old-delta injection.
affected_contracts: Build governance rebaseline activation delta provenance
